messages:
alex-support: FYI into escalation — customer (AcmeCorp) says their account still shows data after they requested a 30-day deletion window. They requested key rotation / HSM key delete as part of the purge. Ticket TKT-8934 attached.

jenn-cust-succ: they submitted a support deletion request via the console on 2026-02-14 17:02 UTC, asked for custom retention shorter than default. says purge not completed. :confused:

mike-security: I pulled audit logs for their org id. Retention-bot shows a pending KMS operation at 2026-02-14T17:05Z: `kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion` but status is "PendingProtectionRemoval" — looks like key pending a 7-day waiting period?

retention-bot: Audit export link: <https://internal.redwood/audit/exports/8934> — export generated, 2.3MB, includes `kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion` events and `data:DeleteRequest` events.

sam-infra: quick note: when a key is scheduled for deletion in our HSM/KMS, cloud policy may enforce a 7-30 day recovery window depending on key policy. If the key is the only wrapping key for stored blobs, we can't decrypt to perform a logical deletion until the key is actually removed or rewrapped.

jenn-cust-succ: customer claims they were told by sales they could get an expedited deletion for PII within 48 hours for enterprise customers. Need confirmation on SLA.

mike-security: legal / compliance will need to weigh in. Laura, can you confirm whether we have an internal exception path for emergency data deletes that involve key escrow / rewrap?

laura-legal: We do have an emergency data deletion policy but it requires: verified requester, signed DPA amendment, and KMS authorization ticket. It does not override external KMS provider enforced recovery windows. We can request a vendor-side expedited recovery but no guarantee. Need the customer signed form and SSO verification.

alex-support: customer shared logs and a short repro: 1) Console > Org > Data & Privacy > Request deletion (custom: 30d) 2) Clicked "Request Key Rotation and Deletion" 3) Received confirmation email 4) After 72h some objects still readable via API. They attached sample API call showing GET /v1/objects/<id> returning 200 and payload.

sam-infra: can you paste the exact API response (scrubbed) and object id? Also which model/artifact type (embeddings/blobs) — rewrap procedure differs.

jenn-cust-succ: pasted (scrubbed) response: `{"id":"obj_7f9b","status":"active","created_at":"2025-11-03T12:01:02Z","payload":"<redacted>"}` — customer says object type = embeddings store.

mike-security: embeddings are encrypted with a per-org data key wrapped by KMS. If KMS delete is still pending protection, the wrapping key may still be usable by internal authorized service account. Need to check key state in KMS console: `gcloud kms keys describe` / `aws kms describe-key` depending on provider.

ops-oncall: I checked provider: key state = PendingDeletion with `PendingWindowInDays=7`, but our internal rotation job still has cached DEK (data-encryption-key) for 48h for background flushes. There's a background cache window we forgot to reduce for enterprise delete flows. That explains the 72h visibility.

alex-support: OK — so root cause likely cached DEK + provider deletion window. Action items?

mike-security: propose steps: 1) Stop DEK-cache for this org immediately (we can set `org.devops.cache_ttl=0`), 2) Mark objects as logically deleted in metadata table (so GET returns 404), 3) Begin vendor expedited recovery request if customer insists on physical wipe before provider window. All require auth from legal and signed customer request.

laura-legal: I'll prepare the DPA amendment template and the vendor escalation authorization. Jenn, get signed form and org SSO proof.

jenn-cust-succ: told customer next steps and asked for signed form. They've started internal sign-off and asked if we can do the cache TTL change now to stop further access.

sam-infra: I'm ready to flip `org.devops.cache_ttl=0` for acct `acme-org-21`. Running command: `infractl org update acme-org-21 --cache-ttl=0` — will deploy in 2 minutes.

ops-oncall: FYI runbook: DATA-DELETE-ESCALATION v3 — link <https://internal.redwood/runbooks/DATA-DELETE-ESCALATION>. Contains checklist for KMS vendor request and evidence collection.

alex-support: thanks team. I'll keep thread updated. Jenn, mark TKT-8934 as high priority and add steps we've agreed.

jenn-cust-succ: done. customer replied :thumbsup: and will send signed DPA within 24h. They also asked about retention default — can we provide the default deletion timeline for new customers?

mike-security: default retention = 90 days for logs/artifacts, 365 days for backups, but data store artifacts follow org-level retention which defaults to 180 days. I'll paste doc link: <https://internal.redwood/docs/data-retention-policies>.

alex-support: closing loop: cache TTL flip scheduled, legal prepping forms, vendor escalation only after signed form. Will update after infra deploy completes. :white_check_mark:
